<reason>A won the comparative argument without defending impunity. B offered credible proportionality analogies and a complementary-tool rationale, but overstated what recognition itself supplies in jurisdiction and enforcement. A directly answered both pressure questions, corrected the alleged domestic-law concession, and exposed B’s retreat from categorical protection for permitted projects to permits being merely evidence. The resulting development-policy uncertainty remained unresolved, while B did not adequately distinguish its proposed accountability gains from those available through coordinated enforcement of specified environmental offenses.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between removing official-capacity immunity and establishing jurisdiction directly undermined B’s promised access to protected perpetrators. B’s closing treated this as demanding guaranteed arrests rather than answering the missing jurisdictional step.</best_rebuttal>
